course_profile.one_sentence_summary: An applied Python-centered NLP course that moves from text acquisition and preprocessing to semantic analysis and introductory neural methods, with progressive laboratory implementation tasks and a project practicum.
course_profile.short_summary: The course is positioned as a continuation of Data Science and is designed to develop the ability to synthesize and verify mathematical models and build specialized software for natural language processing. The accessible materials show a progressive structure: text acquisition and filtering, tokenization and normalization, vectorization and POS analysis, frequency/probabilistic and semantic analysis, classification, similarity, sentiment, and neural-network-based text analysis; the official syllabus then extends this trajectory into audio, GPT-supported NLP, and a project practicum, although those later source documents were not uploaded.

theoretical_understanding: Explain the main stages of an NLP pipeline, from data acquisition and noise filtering to syntactic and semantic analysis.
Differentiate tokenization, stop-word removal, lemmatization, stemming, vectorization, POS tagging, clustering, classification, similarity analysis, and sentiment analysis.
Describe the role of artificial neural network architectures in NLP, including feedforward, recurrent, LSTM/GRU, CNN, and transformer-based approaches.
practical_implementation: Build Python scripts that collect text data, preprocess it, and persist intermediate and final outputs in files.
Implement end-to-end workflows for vectorization, POS-aware analysis, clustering, classification, text similarity, and sentiment analysis.
Prototype introductory neural-network-based solutions for text comparison and sentiment-related tasks on domain-specific corpora.
analysis_validation: Interpret frequency patterns, top words, comparative source differences, and sentiment distributions in collected corpora.
Verify correctness of script implementations and compare alternative technologies or approaches when required by the assignment format.
Assess whether extracted keywords, clusters, or sentiment outputs are aligned with the underlying topic or domain.
architecture_design: Select or synthesize an appropriate mathematical model for an NLP task.
Represent solution structure through a block diagram, structural scheme, or class diagram for at least part of the neural-methods workflow.
Organize progressive functionality growth across an NLP project rather than implementing a single isolated script.
research_and_prototyping: Prototype applied text-analysis solutions in domains such as news, job postings, e-commerce, and real estate.
Use available datasets or scraped corpora to test different text-analysis approaches.
Justify a practical technology choice through comparative analysis when multiple approaches are implemented.

what_student_can_understand: How a practical NLP pipeline is structured from raw text acquisition to semantic and neural analysis.
Why different preprocessing and representation choices matter for downstream text analysis tasks.
How similarity, classification, sentiment analysis, and neural text models relate to one another.
what_student_can_build: Python scripts that scrape, clean, normalize, vectorize, and analyze text corpora.
Small applied NLP projects for domain scenarios such as news analysis, job-market analysis, e-commerce review analysis, or real-estate text analysis.
Introductory neural-network-based prototypes for text comparison and sentiment-oriented tasks.
what_student_can_apply: Text preprocessing and feature engineering for real textual data.
Clustering, classification, similarity, and sentiment workflows on collected corpora.
Verification and comparative evaluation of alternative NLP implementations for practical use cases.
